title: A rocket that didn't go perfectly still built the foundation for everything after. September 29, 2026.
excerpt: From an imperfect first rocket launch to a record that keeps getting broken by the same player, September 29's five stories share one thread: none of them are single moments. All of them are decades of the same work, still compounding.
bodyHtml:
Every story today is really about time doing the work that a single moment couldn't - a rocket's rough first flight setting up three decades of reliable ones, a batting record broken again after seventeen years of the same discipline, a father's 1946 arrival paying off eighty years later, an equipment maker's twenty-five year relationship with India turning into its biggest single bet, and one exam result opening a career that's still going eleven years later.

September 29, 1997: India launched its own rocket, carrying its own satellite, for the first time

PSLV-C1 lifted off from Sriharikota on September 29, 1997, in the first operational flight of India's own Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, carrying the IRS-1D satellite. A helium leak left the satellite in a lower orbit than planned, but IRS-1D still operated for over 12 years - more than a decade past its design life. PSLV itself went on to become one of the most reliable launch vehicles in the world, now flying satellites for dozens of countries.

He's scored more ODI centuries than anyone in history. He just broke his own record again

Virat Kohli scored an unbeaten 139 against West Indies on September 27, 2026, for his 55th ODI century - his century arriving off just 74 balls, the third-fastest of his career. In the same innings he passed 15,000 career ODI runs, becoming only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to reach the mark, and doing it in fewer innings than anyone before him.

His father emigrated from Punjab to study at this college in 1946. In 2026, his son paid off its graduating class's loans

At NC State's Wilson College of Textiles commencement on May 8, 2026, Anil Kochhar and his wife Marilyn surprised graduates by paying off the final-year loans of the whole 2025-26 class - 176 bachelor's and 26 master's recipients. Kochhar's father, Prakash Chand Kochhar, emigrated from Punjab, India to Raleigh in 1946 to study textile manufacturing at the same college, earning degrees there in 1950 and 1952.

A US chip-equipment giant just committed 10,000 crore rupees to India - for silicon nobody's made here before

On September 16, 2026, Lam Research announced it will build India's first silicon component manufacturing facility, backing a vertically integrated process from silicon ingots onward, supporting advanced semiconductor technologies including leading-edge nodes. It builds on the company's 25-year presence in India, and includes a partnership with the Indian Institute of Science to train up to 60,000 students.

His father drove an autorickshaw. His mother worked the fields. At 21, he became one of India's youngest IAS officers

Ansar Shaikh was born in Shelgaon village, Jalna district, Maharashtra, to an autorickshaw driver and an agricultural laborer. He scored 91% in Class 10, graduated in Political Science from Fergusson College, Pune, and in 2016, at age 21, cleared the UPSC Civil Services Examination on his first attempt with All India Rank 361 - becoming one of India's youngest IAS officers, now serving as Additional District Magistrate of Malda, West Bengal.

Five stories, one thread: a rocket's imperfect debut that still launched three decades of reliability, a batting record that keeps compounding one innings at a time, a father's 1946 arrival that took eighty years to fully pay forward, a twenty-five-year relationship that became a landmark commitment, and one UPSC result that's still producing a career eleven years later. Nothing here was a single event. Everything here was time, doing what a single moment never could.
